newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re details terms for French reinsurer sale.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re details terms for French reinsurer sale.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said it would sell Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR) to Bermuda-based PartnerRe Ltd after it completed the ongoing acquisition of the Paris-based European reinsurer.

Swiss Re, which currently holds a 21.6 percent stake in SAFR and 11.1 percent in PartnerRe, said in a statement on Monday it would make a capital gain of 100 million Swiss francs from the deal, which was valued at $950 million by PartnerRe in New York.
Company officials were not available for comment on Monday, a public holiday.
Following the complicated deal, Swiss Re would boost its stake in PartnerRe to 21.8 percent, the statement said.
It said Swiss Re intended to buy SAFR shares it did not already own from Assurances Generales de France (AGF) and Athena, a unit of Worms et Cie.
Swiss Re had said in February that it intended to buy the 78 percent of SAFR shares it did not already own -- 57 percent from AGF and Athena and 21 percent from the public.
The company's statement said it would make a cash tender offer to the public shareholders after it completed the acquisition of shares from AGF and Athena group.

Following this move, if Swiss Re owned at least 95 percent of SAFR's shares, it would then make a repurchase offer for the remaining shares at a price of 1,470 French francs per share, the same price that would be paid to AGF and Atena.
SAFR's shares were quoted on the Paris stock market last Thursday at 1,445 French francs each, sharply up from 935 at the start of January and 850 this time last year.

Under the terms of the deal, PartnerRe would acquire the shares at the same price, the statement said. Swiss Re's 21.6 percent holding in SAFR would be worth 212 million French francs and an unspecified number of newly issued PartnerRe shares.
The statement said Swiss Re would also agree to limit its stake in PartnerRe to a maximum 30 percent.

Earlier on Monday in New York, PartnerRe Ltd said it would pay a total price of 5.4 billion French francs or $950 million for SAFR -- about $800 million in cash and 6.45 million PartnerRe common shares.
SAFR, founded in 1884, writes both life and non-life business and in 1995 recorded profits of some $57 million.

PartnerRe provides, through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Partner Reinsurance Company Ltd, catastrophe reinsurance to insurance companies on a worldwide basis. Risks reinsured include windstorm, earthquake, floods, fires and explosions.
